READABILITY.evidence: Names like encodeIndexShape and readFiniteFloat64 say what they do, but roughly 750 added lines have almost no comments. Single-letter locals carry business logic (`l := &Loop{...}`, `p := &Polygon{...}`, `pl`, `pv`), and the duplicated literal `10` default is never explained.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: All ~750 lines are appended to shapeindex.go instead of a dedicated shapeindex_encode.go. It ignores the existing typeTag mechanism (adds its own shapeKind* constants) and per-shape encode methods (re-serializes Polygon/Polyline ad hoc). decodeShape is one large switch, very likely over 100 lines.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Validation is strong: lengths bounded before allocating, CRC trailer, strict bools, NaN checks, edge/shape ID range checks. But the `maxEdgesPerCell <= 0 { = 10 }` magic is duplicated, and applyUpdatesInternal now wipes cellMap under new conditions. crossing_edge_query picks a shape by looping over the map.

C7-11-CASE1.evidence: Encode/Decode are additive. typeTag values, existing per-shape wire formats and the Shape interface are unchanged. It does change behaviour of existing types along the way: LaxLoop.ChainEdge, LaxPolygon.ChainPosition, PointVector.ChainEdge, and Polyline.decode now takes *decoder.
